summary:
w207 (work-queue r34-r39): research done; notes in .shop/scratch/1-research/notes.md.
All 7 accepted scenarios pass today (run by node id). None is red, so no step or code is missing for them.
Probes (run, scratch repos): list and show of empty, waiting, malformed, and refused targets.
Defect D1: work show <initiative> crashes with a traceback on a non-UTF-8 ledger.md (workqueue_status.ledger).
Defect D2 (reading to settle): work list --json omits the waiting initiative that the text list prints.
Defect D3: a work-item with no kind is refused as 'w9 is a None'.
Old assumptions: work status and the no-target show are retired in the spec but live in code; hook, tests and requests r13/r14 still use them.
No tracked Python file is over 300 lines; git status is clean.
Branch review 3's fix-now finding 2 (supervise_change.py merge) is outside r34-r39; see questions.
No coverage map existed, so every test list is by search.
questions: The accepted scenarios already pass. Does w207 fix branch review 3's findings (D1, D2, D3), which are not scenarios, or only r34-r39? Its findings file also lists fix-now finding 2 in scripts/supervise_change.py, which r34-r39 do not cover.
D2: must work list --json carry the waiting initiative (r39 applies to list in any form), or is the JSON of r35 only the statuses (r35 read literally)?

Retiring work status (decision 0072) conflicts with live requests r13 (work show prints requests), requests r14 (work status prints observations) and migration-tools r32 (the SessionStart hook gives work status). Are these to be replaced before the retirement lands?
The live r7 scenario at features/work-queue.feature:268 uses the no-target work show; removing that branch needs that scenario rewritten. Which?
